name: Sacrococcygeal Teratoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnosis of Sacrococcygeal Teratoma

criteria.description: Presence of a palpable mass in the sacrococcygeal region at or shortly after birth
Imaging evidence (ultrasound, MRI, or CT) showing a heterogeneous mass with cystic and solid components in the sacrococcygeal area
Histopathological confirmation of teratomatous tissue after surgical excision
Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels consistent with teratoma activity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a palpable sacrococcygeal mass with confirmatory imaging and histopathological analysis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Prenatal ultrasound can detect SCT in utero; AFP levels aid in monitoring but are not diagnostic alone.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically a visible or palpable tumor at the base of the spine
searchTerms: mass near tailbone found at birth
lump on lower back detected in newborn

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cystic and solid tumor components on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic heterogeneous appearance on ultrasound or MRI
searchTerms: tumor with fluid and solid parts on scan
mixed cystic and solid mass seen in imaging
complex tumor structure on ultrasound or MRI

common.symptomName: Lower limb weakness or neurological deficits
common.notes: Due to mass effect or spinal cord involvement

searchTerms: difficulty urinating or loss of bladder control

common.notes: Due to mass effect on rectum

common.symptomName: Skin discoloration or ulceration over the mass
common.notes: May indicate tumor necrosis or infection
searchTerms: skin color changes or sores on mass
discolored or ulcerated skin over lump

occasional.notes: Due to high-output cardiac failure from tumor vascularity

searchTerms: too much amniotic fluid in pregnancy
excess fluid around fetus before birth

occasional.notes: In older children or adults with delayed diagnosis

occasional.symptomName: Infection or abscess formation within the tumor
occasional.notes: May complicate untreated or ulcerated tumors

rare.notes: Occurs in older children or untreated cases

searchTerms: severe hemorrhage due to tumor break

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to mass effect in large tumors
rare.notes: Rare but possible in neonates with very large SCT
searchTerms: respiratory distress caused by mass effect
difficulty breathing due to tumor size

imaging: Ultrasound showing mixed cystic and solid sacrococcygeal mass
MRI delineating tumor extent and relation to spinal canal
CT scan for surgical planning and metastasis evaluation
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology demonstrating tissues from all three germ layers
Presence of mature or immature teratomatous elements

distinguishingFeatures: Neural tube defect with exposed spinal cord tissue
Associated neurological deficits present at birth
Lacks the complex tissue types seen in teratoma
Usually covered by skin without large external mass
Small cyst or abscess near the coccyx
No solid tumor components or germ layer tissues
Typically presents later in adolescence or adulthood

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of sacrococcygeal mass
Signs of high-output cardiac failure in neonate
Ulceration or bleeding from the tumor surface
references: Luzzatto C, et al. Sacrococcygeal teratoma: diagnosis and management. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2020.

Kaufman RA, et al. Imaging of sacrococcygeal teratomas. Radiographics. 2018.
